task.description: Produce the design artefact for REQ-228 (entity event registration and record commands), resolving the named open design question and specifying the transaction-boundary and idempotency-lookup mechanisms.

result.note: Design doc written to lib/letflow/design/req228-entity-event-registration-commands.md (634 lines). Named open design question resolved: synthetic instances are per-entity-TYPE, not per-record, matching R-Co's shipped commands.zig, justified on unbounded-vs-bounded row growth and entity records having no terminal-state lifecycle. Transaction-boundary design: discovered Letflow.EventStore.append/2 commits its own transaction internally, so cannot host an extra entity_record_latest write in the same commit -- design proposes a new, purely-additive Letflow.EventStore.append_multi/3 (mirroring the existing Letflow.Engine.TaskActivation.append_multi/6 'extend a caller-supplied open Multi' idiom) factoring out append/2's steps without opening/committing a transaction itself; Letflow.Entities.Records's command functions then compose one Ecto.Multi (entity_type_instance_guard -> append_multi/3's steps -> upsert_record_latest) and call Repo.transaction/1 exactly once, satisfying AC2's atomicity requirement. Idempotency-lookup design: reuses REQ-024's existing event_idempotency sidecar exactly as append/2's own claim_idempotency/resolve_duplicate already do -- no new table; on a duplicate idempotency_key, the original Event.payload (already containing entity_type/record_id/field_values) is decoded and returned directly, guaranteeing ISS-0159/GH#480 parity. Self-checked: grepped for defmodule/def-with-body/schema-do patterns and scanned every fenced block for executable-looking lines -- zero matches, all fenced blocks are @type/@spec only.
